source: TSTD/MAFF Pumpkin (ល្ពៅ) Cultivation Manual, PDF title "10_Pumpkin_manual_body+covers" (TSTD — TA 7305-CAM), 2012
text: Several insect/mite pests are covered for pumpkin. Leaf beetles (an orange/golden beetle shown feeding on leaves in the source's photos) chew irregular holes in leaves and can damage seedlings badly if numbers are high; scouting fields regularly and removing/controlling beetles early is recommended. Aphids (ព្រុយ) cluster on shoots and the undersides of leaves, sucking sap and stunting growth, and can also spread plant viruses -- the source's photos reference at least three named viral symptom patterns in the field (labeled in the images as NMK, PRSV, and ZYMV), consistent with common cucurbit-infecting viruses (e.g. papaya ringspot virus and zucchini yellow mosaic virus are globally documented cucurbit viruses transmitted by aphids -- exact strain identification from a farmer's field photo would need expert/lab confirmation, not a symptom guess). Whitefly (រុយស white/pale small flying insect) similarly feeds on the underside of leaves and is a documented vector for cucurbit leaf curl viruses. Mites (ព្រុយ/red spider-mite type) cause stippling and leaf curling on the underside of leaves in hot, dry conditions. For chemical control, the source names abamectin, cypermethrin+chlorpyrifos, imidacloprid, and thiomethoxam as insecticide/miticide active ingredients used against these pests -- as with disease control, exact dosage rates and safety intervals should be verified against the current registered product label before advising a farmer, since precise numeric detail in the surrounding text could not be confidently read from the corrupted source.
caveat: Chemical active-ingredient names (abamectin, cypermethrin, chlorpyrifos, imidacloprid, thiomethoxam) and the virus-label abbreviations shown in source photos (NMK, PRSV, ZYMV) were legible with reasonable confidence. The full Khmer names/descriptions of each named pest, and exact application rates, were not reliably extractable due to the same font-corruption issue affecting the rest of this document -- treat pest descriptions here as functional summaries, not verbatim source text, and confirm any specific pesticide product/rate with a current agricultural extension source before use.
